title: India showcases UHC progress and Sickle Cell elimination goals at UNGA81
summary: India highlighted its progress in Universal Health Coverage (UHC) and launched the OneSCD partnership for sickle cell care at the 81st UN General Assembly. Key achievements reported include the establishment of over 1.8 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, the creation of 900 million+ Unique Health IDs, and 497 million+ teleconsultations via e-Sanjeevani. Additionally, India reiterated its commitment to Hepatitis elimination by 2030 and set a target for Sickle Cell elimination by 2047 through the newly launched OneSCD global partnership to ensure equitable and accessible care.

title: Launch of 7th National Formulary of India 2026 and Biovigilance Programme
summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has launched the 7th National Formulary of India (NFI) 2026 and the Biovigilance Programme of India. Led by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), the Biovigilance Programme will monitor adverse events linked to organ and tissue transplantation. Key updates include the launch of the ADR-PvPI 2.0 Mobile App for iOS and a new guidance document for reporting medical device-related adverse events. India's global rank in the WHO patient safety database has improved from 123rd to 8th. Currently, approximately 1,150 ADR Reporting Centres are operational, with plans to expand to the primary healthcare level. The 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week (17–23 September 2026) is themed “Promoting Rational Use of Medicines through Pharmacovigilance: A Step Towards Safer Healthcare.”

title: Union Health Ministry Observes World Patient Safety Day 2026 with Focus on NCDs
summary: The Union Health Ministry commemorated World Patient Safety Day 2026 with the theme “Safe Care for Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs).” The observance emphasized the need for a structured, time-bound approach to quality assurance across the continuum of NCD prevention, diagnosis, and long-term management. Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director (NHM), highlighted that nearly 63% of all deaths in India are attributed to NCDs, making patient safety a critical component of healthcare delivery to address this growing burden.

title: Mandatory CCTV proposed for medical stores selling Schedule H, H1, and X drugs
summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed mandatory CCTV surveillance at medical stores to strengthen regulatory oversight of Schedule H, H1, and X drugs. Under Draft Gazette Notification G.S.R. 791 (E) dated September 8, 2026, the proposed amendments to the Drugs Rules, 1945, aim to curb unauthorized access and the sale of these drugs without valid prescriptions. The proposal, which was recommended by the Drugs Technical Advisory Board (DTAB), seeks to enhance transparency and accountability across the pharmaceutical supply chain. The Ministry is currently inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders regarding this regulatory safeguard.

title: Stem cell therapy restricted to Ministry-approved indications and clinical trials for ASD
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has issued an advisory restricting stem cell therapy as standard care to only those disease conditions included in the Ministry-approved list. Following a Supreme Court judgment (Yash Charitable Trust v. Union of India), the therapeutic use of stem cells for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is now strictly limited to approved clinical trials in accordance with the National Guidelines for Stem Cell Research, 2017, issued by ICMR and DBT. Unproven stem cell interventions must not be offered as routine or commercial clinical services. This advisory applies to all States and UTs that have adopted the Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010.

title: 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week Launched to Promote Rational Medicine Use
summary: The 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week is being observed across India from September 17–23, 2026, themed “Promoting Rational Use of Medicines through Pharmacovigilance – A Step Towards Safer Healthcare.” Organized by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), which serves as the National Coordination Centre for the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (NCC-PvPI), the campaign aims to sensitize healthcare professionals and the public on Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) reporting. The initiative focuses on strengthening grassroots pharmacovigilance networks to better inform regulatory and clinical actions.

title: Quality & Safety Handbook Released for World Patient Safety Day 2026
summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare released the Quality & Safety Handbook at Dr. RML Hospital to strengthen patient safety practices on World Patient Safety Day 2026. The theme for 2026 is “Safe care for noncommunicable diseases” with the slogan “Safe care for life!”. Union Health Minister J.P. Nadda highlighted key health milestones, noting that Ayushman Bharat has enabled 11.5 crore beneficiaries to access treatment worth approximately ₹1.6 lakh crore, and Jan Aushadhi has saved citizens around ₹45,000 crore on medicines. The initiative focuses on integrating safe, coordinated, and continuous care for patients with NCDs into the broader health-system strengthening framework.

title: Union Health Minister Inaugurates 10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 IPHLs in Andhra Pradesh
summary: Union Health Minister Shri J P Nadda inaugurated 10 Critical Care Blocks (CCBs) and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories (IPHLs) in Andhra Pradesh. These facilities are part of the PM-ABHIM (Prime Minister Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission), which has sanctioned 631 CCBs nationwide to enhance pandemic response and critical care capacity. The inaugurated blocks are located at GMCs in Kadapa, Nellore, Srikakulam, Visakhapatnam, Ongole, Rajamahendravaram, Kurnool, and SMC Vijaya, and District Hospitals in Anakapalli and Hindupur. Additionally, the Minister highlighted Andhra Pradesh's Sanjeevani programme, which facilitates doorstep healthcare and testing for 41 health parameters to strengthen the linkage between preventive and tertiary care.

title: India Administers 8 Million HPV Vaccine Doses Under National Campaign
summary: India has administered over 80 lakh (8 million) doses of the HPV vaccine under the National HPV Vaccination Campaign since its launch in February 2026. The initiative provides free, voluntary single-dose HPV vaccination to 14-year-old girls at government health facilities with parental consent. Based on RGI 2021 estimates, the annual target cohort is approximately 1.2 crore girls. Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Mizoram have achieved 100% coverage, while Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Assam have exceeded 90%. Uttar Pradesh leads with over 22 lakh vaccinations. All sessions are conducted under medical supervision with 24x7 arrangements for the management of Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI).

title: IPC Launches Reference Substance for Enoxaparin Sodium
summary: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC) has launched the Indian Pharmacopoeia Reference Substance (IPRS) for Enoxaparin Sodium for bioassays. This announcement was made during a two-day National Conference on "Quality and Safety of Biosimilars: Strengthening India’s Biopharma SHAKTI Vision" held on September 10–11, 2026, in Bengaluru. The initiative aligns with the government's Biopharma SHAKTI Vision to enhance the biopharmaceutical ecosystem through innovation and self-reliance. The conference, attended by 160 stakeholders, addressed critical regulatory and scientific challenges including pharmacopoeial standards, analytical characterization, immunogenicity, and pharmacovigilance to ensure the quality and safety of biosimilars in India.

title: Union Health Ministry holds National Workshop to strengthen NPPCF
summary: The Union Health Ministry organized a National Multi-Stakeholder Workshop on Fluorosis to strengthen the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Fluorosis (NPPCF). The workshop focused on enhancing the prevention, early detection, management, and control of fluorosis through research, innovation, and multisectoral action. Key stakeholders involved included the Ministry of Jal Shakti, ICAR, ICMR, AIIMS, and the National Dental Commission. The primary objectives discussed were expanding the reach and coverage of the NPPCF and improving real-time information sharing and coordination across diverse sectors to effectively combat the condition.

title: India reports >175% increase in MBBS/PG seats and adopts Dili Declaration on Specialized Care
summary: India has significantly expanded its medical education infrastructure, increasing MBBS and PG seats by over 175% since 2014. During the 79th WHO Regional Committee Session (RC79), Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda highlighted that medical colleges have more than doubled to improve equitable access to specialized care for rural, tribal, and underserved populations. The WHO South-East Asia Region adopted the Dili Declaration on Equity in Specialized Care. Furthermore, India was honored with two WHO South-East Asia Regional Awards for its sustained leadership in Maternal Health and Noncommunicable Disease (NCD) management.

title: MoHFW Launches SUMAN Roadmap 2030 to Eliminate Preventable Maternal and Newborn Deaths
summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has initiated the SUMAN Roadmap 2030 to accelerate the continuum of care and achieve zero preventable maternal and newborn deaths. The strategy specifically targets 13 high-focus states and 130 districts with tailored interventions for vulnerable and underserved areas. A key component highlighted is the registration of newly married couples to prevent unintended pregnancies and promote planned, healthy pregnancies. The roadmap emphasizes ensuring safe, respectful, and quality maternal and newborn healthcare across the continuum.

title: UGC Standardizes Allied and Healthcare Education via 'One Nation, One Curriculum'
summary: The University Grants Commission (UGC) has notified 33 new and 21 restructured undergraduate and postgraduate degrees under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions (NCAHP) regulatory framework. This initiative, published in the Gazette on August 31, 2026, implements the 'One Nation, One Curriculum' mandate to ensure uniformity in course duration, degree nomenclature, and entry qualifications nationwide. The move aims to strengthen professional standards and build a competent, future-ready allied healthcare workforce through the 5th Amendment to the Specification of Degrees under the UGC Act, 1956.
